newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Nasdaq composite flirts with key support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Nasdaq composite flirts with key support.

text.p: The Nasdaq composite, which has lagged the performance of the Dow industrials, is flirting with key support levels, technical analysts said on Tuesday.

Some analysts noted the Nasdaq composite on Monday bounced above its 50-day moving average at about 1332, a bullish sign for the index. The Nasdaq composite was up about three points at 1349 on Tuesday afternoon.
But others point to the 1320 level on the Nasdaq composite as a point, that if breached, could lead to a further downtrend.

"If the (Nasdaq) market continues to lag, and it does break 1320, then I think odds would favor the weakness spilling over into big cap stocks," said Ricky Harrington, tech analyst, Interstate/Johnson Lane.
While the Dow smashed through the 7000 level this month, the Nasdaq index has been weighed down by weakness in technology stocks, particularly computer networking shares.
The Nasdaq index last saw a record high on January 22, when it closed at 1388.

The Nasdaq's index's ability to find technical support would help offset other technical negatives, such as its being out of sync with other indices, including the Dow, said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities.
Nie cited 1330 as "key support" for the Nasdaq index.
Gary Kaltbaum, technical analyst at J.W. Charles/CSG, said the Nasdaq composite could pull back to the 1300 level but had "plenty of support" in the 1250-1300 area.
While computer networking shares have been hit in recent weeks, market heavyweights including Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp have been relatively solid, he said.
"Unless Intel really starts cratering and Microsoft starts cratering, I think probably the Nasdaq holds up," Kaltbaum said.
But Harrington said that big capitalization stocks such as Intel and Microsoft have "distorted" the Nasdaq composite's performance by masking weakness in a broader number of Nasdaq shares.
He said market breadth for Nasdaq, as measured by the daily advance/decline line, peaked about a year ago and has been in a "protracted downtrend."
Harrington cited the potential for a "serious correction," or at least a protracted trading range, if 1320 is broken to the downside on the Nasdaq composite.
